name: Make It Increasing
description: You are given an array of $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_n$$$, and a set $$$b$$$ of $$$k$$$ distinct integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. In one operation, you may choose two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$x$$$ can be any integer) and assign $$$a_i := x$$$. This operation can be done only if $$$i$$$ does not belong to the set $$$b$$$. Calculate the minimum number of operations you should perform so the array $$$a$$$ is increasing (that is, $$$a_1 \lt a_2 \lt a_3 \lt \dots \lt a_n$$$), or report that it is impossible.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le k \le n$$$) — the size of the array $$$a$$$ and the set $$$b$$$, respectively. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). Then, if $$$k \ne 0$$$, the third line follows, containing $$$k$$$ integers $$$b_1$$$, $$$b_2$$$, ..., $$$b_k$$$ ($$$1 \le b_1 \lt b_2 \lt \dots \lt b_k \le n$$$). If $$$k = 0$$$, this line is skipped .
output_specification: If it is impossible to make the array $$$a$$$ increasing using the given operations, print $$$-1$$$. Otherwise, print one integer — the minimum number of operations you have to perform.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
